So, ALMA. I know the name. Which part of the firm do you sit in?
I lead the practice that advises financial institutions: banks, payment companies and funds that operate in Brazil.
Payments. That is the part of your reform I do not understand at all. Give me a client.
Take one that we onboarded in March. A payment group whose holding is in Luxembourg, with two operating companies that run the business in Brazil and Mexico.
And the money leaves Brazil how?
Through a fourth entity, which nobody talks about, domiciled in the Cayman Islands. Every remittance passes through it.
There it is. That is the subsidiary your authority will look at first.
It already has. The exemption they claim depends on a provision that the tax authority is now reading in a different way.
Is that a gray area, or is it simply wrong?
A gray area. The provision has never been tested in court, and the partner who signed the original opinion has left the firm.
Welcome to my life. Half of my files are provisions that nobody has ever challenged.

Leonardo, it is Paulo, from the corporate team. I am sending you the structure of the client that we onboarded in March, because you will need it before the trip. The group has four entities. The holding, which was incorporated in Luxembourg, owns everything below it. Then there are two operating companies that run the payment business, one in Brazil and one in Mexico. And there is a fourth entity, a small one that nobody remembers, domiciled in the Cayman Islands. That fourth one is the problem. Every remittance that leaves Brazil passes through it, and the exemption they have been claiming since 2021 depends on a provision that the tax authority is now reading in a different way. The partner who signed the original opinion has left the firm, so we cannot ask him. My recommendation is simple. Do not describe this group as four companies. Describe it as one holding, two operating companies, and one entity that needs a decision this quarter. Call me if the jurisdiction of the Cayman entity comes up, because that is the part I would not improvise.

I want to tell you about the question that changed how I speak to clients. Early in my career I described a group structure to an American partner, and I did it the way we all do at the beginning. One fact, full stop. Another fact, full stop. The client has a subsidiary. The subsidiary is in the Cayman Islands. It has an exposure. He listened politely, and then he asked me, very gently, whether I actually understood the structure or whether I was reading it from a page. That question stayed with me for years. The problem was not my English. My words were correct, my grammar was correct. The problem was that I was giving him a list, and a list does not show relationships. What a partner wants to hear is which company matters, which rule applies to it, and where the risk sits. So now I build one sentence with all of it. The client has a subsidiary in the Cayman Islands, which carries a significant exposure under the provision we are challenging. Same information, one breath, and suddenly you sound like the person who knows the file.

The group is led by a holding company, which is domiciled in Luxembourg. Below it there are two operating companies that run the payment business. There is also a fourth entity, which is domiciled in the Cayman Islands. Every remittance that leaves Brazil passes through that entity. The exemption they claim depends on a provision that the authority is now challenging.
